title: Chapter 7 — The AI-Assisted Appliance Salesperson
intro: AI is a tool — not a replacement. This chapter explains what AI does well, what it must never do, and how it makes you better at the parts of selling that are uniquely human.

sections.title: AI Is Your Verification Partner
sections.content:
One of the principles in this program is that you should never guess. If you are uncertain about a spec, a delivery date, an installation requirement, or a compatibility question — verify it.

AI changes how verification works. Instead of walking away to search through binders, websites, or brochures, you ask the AI. The customer sees that the answer is being verified against current specifications, inventory, lead times, and compatibility.

You are not pretending to know everything. You are demonstrating that you have access to the best information available. In today's world, that is a stronger form of expertise than relying on memory.

sections.title: What AI Does Well
sections.content:
AI is excellent at things humans find tedious or error-prone: looking up specs instantly, comparing products across dozens of features, checking inventory and delivery windows, calculating financing options, generating follow-up reminders, and analyzing your performance data to show you where to improve.

These are all things that used to take time away from selling. AI handles them so you can spend more time doing the thing that actually closes deals: connecting with the human being in front of you.

sections.title: What AI Must Never Do
sections.content:
AI should never replace the human relationship. Customers buy from people they trust. They do not trust algorithms — they trust the person who listened to them, understood their kitchen, and helped them feel confident about a big purchase.

AI cannot read body language. It cannot sense when a customer is overwhelmed. It cannot adjust its energy to match the mood of the room. It cannot shake a hand, share a laugh, or remember that a customer's daughter just got married.

AI makes you faster and more accurate. The relationship is still yours to build.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating AI integration, ask:

Does the salesperson use AI to verify information — or still guess?
Do they use AI tools to improve their follow-up and preparation?
Do they rely on AI as a tool — or use it as a crutch to avoid learning?
Is the human relationship still at the center of their sales process?

The best AI-assisted salespeople use technology to handle the details so they can focus on the customer.
